content.intro: Learn creating function-based views through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Creating Function-Based Views matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines creating function-based views as part of url routing and views. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Defining a view function; Receiving the request object; Returning a response; Reading request information; Keeping views readable. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Defining a view function
items.text: Defining a view function is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Reading request information
items.text: Reading request information shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
